=== ADMISSION HISTORY AND PHYSICAL ===

--- Chief Complaint ---
Progressive memory loss and functional decline.

--- History of Present Illness ---
82-year-old woman brought by son for 1 year of progressive short-term memory loss, getting lost in her neighborhood, and difficulty managing medications and finances. Over the past month she has had urinary incontinence and two falls. No headache, no weakness, no fever. Son reports she repeats questions frequently.

--- Past Medical History ---
Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, vitamin B12 deficiency.

--- Medications ---
Amlodipine 5 mg daily, Atorvastatin 20 mg nightly, Cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily, Aspirin 81 mg daily.

--- Social History ---
Widowed, lives alone with daily aide. Former teacher. No alcohol. No smoking.

--- Review of Systems ---
Memory loss, incontinence, falls as above. Denies headache, dizziness, weakness, numbness.

--- Physical Exam ---
Vitals: Temp 98.3 F, HR 68, BP 142/78, RR 14, SpO2 98% RA.
Cognitive: MMSE 18/30, deficits in recall and orientation.
Neuro: Gait mildly wide-based, otherwise nonfocal.
General: Pleasant, cooperative.

--- Studies ---
Labs: B12 210 (L), TSH 2.1, RPR nonreactive.
MRI brain: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to atrophy, concerning for normal pressure hydrocephalus.
Neuropsych testing: Pending.

--- Assessment ---
82-year-old woman with progressive cognitive decline and gait disturbance with ventriculomegaly; normal pressure hydrocephalus on the differential.

--- Plan ---
1. Possible normal pressure hydrocephalus
- Neurosurgery consult; consider high-volume lumbar tap test
- Gait and cognitive assessment before/after tap test
2. Vitamin B12 deficiency
- Continue replacement; recheck level in 3 months
3. Fall risk and safety
- PT evaluation, home safety assessment
- Discuss goals of care and decision-making capacity with son
